question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}\,{x}^{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{y}{2}}, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(Y\le 1).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{6}\,{x}^{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{y}{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\sqrt[3]{\frac{y}{2}}{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}\sqrt[3]{\frac{y}{2}}[{2}^{4}-{0}^{4}] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{y}{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{y}{2}}, & 0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le 1) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{1}{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{y}{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,{y}^{1/3}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{2}}{[\frac{3}{4}{y}^{4/3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt[3]{2}}[{1}^{4/3}-{0}^{4/3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt[3]{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
